content.title: Sean Penn Joins the Oscars' Exclusive 3-Timers Club
content.text: Penn won his third Oscar at the 2026 ceremony for his supporting role in ‘One Battle After Another.’Mar 15, 2026 11:10 PM EDTSean Penn joins the Oscars' 3-timers club with his third career Academy Award win for 'One Battle After Another.' Dominique Charriau/WireImageKey PointsSean Penn joins the Oscars' 3-timers club with his third career win..He won this year's award for Best Supporting Actor for "One Battle After Another."Only a select number of other actors have earned 3 Oscars wins, including Ingrid Bergman and Daniel Day-Lewis. Sean Penn is officially in the Oscars’ “3-Timers Club.” At the 98th Academy Awards on Sunday, March 15, Penn was awarded the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor following his performance in Paul Thomas Anderson‘s One Battle After Another. Penn, 65, wasn’t in attendance to accept the award at the ceremony, but his win marks a special accomplishment for the actor, who now joins an elite list of stars with three Oscar wins for acting. Oscars 2026: Full List of Winners How Many Oscars Has Sean Penn Won? Penn has now won three Academy Awards out of six total career nominations. In addition to his Supporting Actor win for One Battle After Another at this year’s awards, Penn previously won Best Lead Actor in 2004 for Mystic River, followed by another win in the same category in 2009 for Milk. His other nominations include lead actor nods in 1996 for Dead Man Walking, 2000 for Sweet and Lowdown and 2002 for I Am Sam. In addition to Penn, these Hollywood stars have also earned an impressive 3 Oscar wins for acting throughout their respective careers: Ingrid Bergman WINS:Gaslight (1945, Best Actress) Anastasia (1957, Best Actress) Murder on the Orient Express (1975, Best Supporting Actress) NOMINATIONS:For Whom the Bell Tolls (1944, Best Actress) The Bells of St. Marys (1946, Best Actress) Joan of Arc (1949, Best Actress) Autumn Sonata (1979, Best Actress) Walter Brennan WINS:Come and Get It (1937, Best Supporting Actor) Kentucky (1939, Best Supporting Actor) The Westerner (1941, Best Supporting Actor) NOMINATIONS:Sergeant York (1942, Best Supporting Actor) Daniel Day-Lewis WINS:My Left Foot (1990, Best Actor) There Will Be Blood (2008, Best Actor) Lincoln (2013, Best Actor NOMINATIONS:In the Name of the Father (1994, Best Actor) Gangs of New York (2003, Best Actor) Phantom Thread (2018, Best Actor) Frances McDormand WINS:Fargo (1997, Best Actress) Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri (2018, Best Actress) Nomadland (2021, Best Actress) NOMINATIONS: Mississippi Burning (1989, Best Supporting Actress) Almost Famous (2001, Best Supporting Actress) North Country (2006, Best Supporting Actress) (McDorman also holds a fourth Oscar for producing 2021 Best Picture winner, Nomadland.) Jack Nicholson WINS:One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest (1976, Best Actor) Terms of Endearment (1984, Best Supporting Actor) As Good as It Gets (1998, Best Actor) NOMINATIONS: Easy Rider (1970, Best Supporting Actor) Five Easy Pieces (1971, Best Actor) The Last Detail (1974, Best Actor) Chinatown (1975, Best Actor) Reds (1982, Best Supporting Actor) Prizzi’s Honor (1986, Best Actor) Ironweed (1988, Best Actor) A Few Good Men (1993, Best Supporting Actor) About Schmidt (2003, Best Actor) Meryl Streep WINS:Kramer vs. Kramer (1980, Best Supporting Actress) Sophie’s Choice (1983, Best Actress) The Iron Lady (2012, Best Actress) NOMINATIONS: The Deer Hunter (1979, Best Supporting Actress) The French Lieutenant’s Woman (1982, Best Actress) Silkwood (1984, Best Actress) Out of Africa (1986, Best Actress) Ironweed (1988, Best Actress) A Cry in the Dark (1989, Best Actress) Postcards from the Edge (1991, Best Actress) The Bridges of Madison County (1996, Best Actress) One True Thing (1999, Best Actress) Music of the Heart (2000, Best Actress) Adaptation (2003, Best Supporting Actress) The Devil Wears Prada (2007, Best Actress) Doubt (2009, Best Actress) Julie and Julia (2010, Best Actress) August: Osage County (2014, Best Actress) Into the Woods (2015, Best Supporting Actress) Florence Foster Jenkins (2017, Best Actress) The Post (2018, Best Actress) Katharine Hepburn Katharine Hepburn is the only person to ever win 4 Oscars for acting. WINS: Morning Glory (1934, Best Actress) Guess Who’s Coming to Dinner (1968, Best Actress) The Lion in Winter (1969, Best Actress) On Golden Pond (1982, Best Actress) NOMINATIONS: Alice Adams (1936, Best Actress) The Philadelphia Story (1941, Best Actress) Woman of the Year (1943, Best Actress) The African Queen (1952, Best Actress) Summertime (1956, Best Actress) The Rainmaker (1957, Best Actress) Suddenly, Last Summer (1960, Best Actress) Long Day’s Journey Into Night (1963, Best Actress) About the authorCarly Silva is a trending news writer for Parade, where she writes articles on the day’s most talked-about topics, ranging from celebrity love lives and award show coverage to social media trends and viral pop culture news.Trending Stories
